summary:
This attempt closes the three owed items and changes nothing else in the design.

- **O-009:** Attempt 3 had answered this case with the wrong test: EngineCases, filed under key C-005. The right test is the sibling test's ExpectFactsMismatch shape, and it now also requires the 'exits 2' CANNOT-READ row under both inner shells. It passes on a tree of N Facts ('found 11 … has 12') and on a tree of N+1 ('found 12 … has 13').
- **O-024:** Both SL-069 guard entries in .taad/fitness.yaml now carry `-ExpectFacts['"]?\s*,\s*['"]?\d`. GuardRule's pinned samples now include the argument-array spellings, and the derived samples now include `@('-ExpectFacts', $facts)` and `@('-ExpectFacts', $more)`, which must not be hit.
- **O-025:** harness.py prints each import-rule name in single quotes instead of the list's repr. C-007 reads yaml names through a new Get-YamlName, which handles single quotes with a doubled `''` and double quotes. A new engine-only shape, ImportRuleNames, adds two import rules with an apostrophe in the name, one quoted each way, to a repo copy. It passes, and it fails when the old repr print is put back.

This is the third build lap in a row caused by obligations landing on build-slice after it had passed. The last one came back only because attempt 3 named the wrong test for O-009.

files.why: O-025: describe_not_run joins each unran import-rule name in single quotes instead of interpolating the list's repr, which double-quoted any name holding an apostrophe.
O-025: new Get-YamlName unwraps a single-quoted name (turning '' into ') or a double-quoted one. C-007's import-rule reader uses it instead of .Trim().Trim("'").

O-024: added `-ExpectFacts['"]?\s*,\s*['"]?\d` to both SL-069 guard entries ('the rule-case suite never pins a literal parity count' and 'the SL-069 count tests never pin a literal parity count'), so each now has 10 patterns.

O-009: ExpectFactsMismatch also requires C-005's 'exits 2' and CANNOT-READ 'found N … has N+1' rows under both inner shells. O-024: GuardRule's pinned samples gain @('-ExpectFacts', '<n>') and @('-ExpectFacts', <n>), built with -f, and its derived samples gain the $facts/$more array forms. O-025: new engine-only shape ImportRuleNames, and the header comment is updated.

obligations.how: The test that feeds this shape is tests/bugs/SL-069-EveryCaseFollowsCounts.Tests.ps1 -Shape ExpectFactsMismatch; attempt 3 had wrongly named EngineCases. It builds an unchanged copy (N Facts) and a copy with one more Fact (N+1), and runs each copy's C-005, which passes -ExpectFacts N+1. It now requires, under both powershell.exe and pwsh inside C-005, the 'exits 2' row and the CANNOT-READ row 'the reader found N Facts where the test class has N+1'. Measured: exit 0 in 125 s, with 'found 11 … has 12' on the unchanged copy and 'found 12 … has 13' on the grown one.

Added `-ExpectFacts['"]?\s*,\s*['"]?\d` to both SL-069 must_not_match lists. Added ("@('-ExpectFacts', '{0}')" -f 11) and ("@('-ExpectFacts', {0})" -f 12) to Shape-GuardRule's $pinned, and the array forms with $facts/$more to $derived. GuardRule exits 0. The rule hits both array samples; only the new regex can match them. It still hits the pre-fix file at exactly 35,240,243,305,326,370,408,600,625,633, and hits nothing in the working RuleCases.ps1 or either SL-069 test. SL-053's GuardRule still holds.

harness.py:describe_not_run now prints `', '.join("'" + name + "'")` instead of `{names}`. RuleCases.ps1 C-007 reads names through Get-YamlName (single-quoted: strip and turn '' into '; double-quoted: strip). New shape ImportRuleNames (needs the engine) appends 'the provider''s helper never imports Core' and "the provider's stub never imports Core" as import rules on a repo copy. C-007 then exits 0 under both shells, with 'the 3 import rule(s) are named NOT RUN … (unnamed: )'. With the old `{names}` print put back temporarily (bytes restored and hash-checked afterwards), the same shape exits 1 and lists both apostrophe names as unnamed, because the harness printed them double-quoted.

tests.note: Exit 0 in 1 s. The rule now has 10 patterns, the same in both entries. Pre-fix hits are 35,240,243,305,326,370,408,600,625,633. It hits nothing in this tree's RuleCases.ps1 or either SL-069 test. It hits @('-ExpectFacts', '11') and @('-ExpectFacts', 12), and does not hit @('-ExpectFacts', $facts) or $more. SettledCountProbe -Shape GuardRule holds.

Exit 0 in 125 s. C-005 holds on the unchanged copy ('found 11 Facts where the test class has 12') and on a copy with one more Fact ('found 12 … has 13'), each with exits-2 rows under powershell.exe and pwsh.

Exit 0 in 68 s. The copy AGREEs at 11/15/27/51, the unchanged tree's line plus two settled entries. C-007 exits 0 under both shells with 'the 3 import rule(s) are named NOT RUN, and the verdict is not pass (unnamed: )'.

tests.command: same ImportRuleNames command with harness.py's describe_not_run temporarily reverted to `{names}` (bytes restored in finally, hash verified)
tests.note: Deliberate mutant, and it failed as intended with exit 1. The harness printed ['the provider does not use the code it checks', "the provider's helper never imports Core", "the provider's stub never imports Core"], and C-007 failed with 'unnamed: the provider's helper never imports Core, the provider's stub never imports Core'. This shows the shape bites on the harness end.

Real tree, exit 0 in 31 s: 'xunit 11 Facts, 0 hits', 'none unmatched', 'the 1 import rule(s) are named NOT RUN … (unnamed: )', and the stray-violation bite holds. The engine parsed the new plain-scalar regex and found 0 hits.
AGREE 11 facts <- 15 twinned entries, 27 patterns; 49 settled entries not compared. Exit 0.
Both exit 0 with 'All checks held.' on the real tree after the yaml and RuleCases edits.
The acceptance repro exits 0 in 5 s: 'OK: RuleCases.ps1 C-001 holds on a tree with one more twinned rule'.

deviations: O-025's fix names only harness.py and RuleCases.ps1. I also added an engine-only shape, ImportRuleNames, to the sibling test so the apostrophe shape is actually fed in; validate had recorded it as not reached. Like EngineCases, it is left out of -Shape All and fails as not reached without -EnginePython/-EngineRoot.
follow_ups: Get-YamlName strips double quotes but does not unescape YAML escapes (\" or \\) inside a double-quoted name, as O-025's fix specified. A must_not_import rule whose double-quoted name contains an escape would still be reported unnamed by C-007.

Loop shape: build-slice has been sent back three times, each time by obligations that landed on it after it had passed (O-021, then O-009/O-024/O-025). O-009 came back only because attempt 3 reported the case under key C-005 with the EngineCases command instead of key C-003 with ExpectFactsMismatch. If case obligations were routed before build passes, a lap could be saved.
